==Drop Locations==
{{DropLocations}}

==Notes==
*For any non-integer magazine values the magazine size is simply rounded to the nearest whole number. For example, a {{Weapon|Strun}} modded with a max rank '''Burdened Magazine''' will have a calculated magazine size of {{Math|6 {{mul}} (1 + 60%)|t=y|bf-a=y}}, which will simply round to {{math|6 {{mul}} (1 + 60%)|round = 1|bf-a = y}}.
*Suitable for shotguns with innately high magazine capacities ({{Weapon|Boar}}, {{Weapon|Boar Prime}}, {{Weapon|Sobek}}, or {{Weapon|Phage}}).
**Could make one magazine last entire fights without needing any reloads, thus nullifying the negative reload speed.
*Combining this mod and {{M|Ammo Stock}} would give +120% magazine size to the modded shotgun.
**Unlike {{M|Tainted Mag}} and {{M|Tainted Clip}}, this mod increases the magazine size just as much as the non-corrupt counterpart, hence it should only be used in conjunction with Ammo Stock in builds aiming to maximize magazine size.
**With this mod and Ammo Stock, {{Weapon|Tigris}} and it's variants can reach a magazine size of 4. With a rank 5 Ammo Stock, Burdened Magazine can be left at rank 1 to minimize the reload penalty and capacity drain.

==Trivia==
*Prior to {{ver|16.7}}, this mod was usable in [[PvP]] games until it was replaced by its own specific PvP mods along with a number of other mods: {{M|Quickdraw}}, {{M|Fast Hands}}, {{M|Slip Magazine}}, {{M|Tactical Pump}}, {{M|Steady Hands}}, {{M|Stabilizer}}, {{M|Magazine Warp}} and {{M|Terminal Velocity}}.

The '''Burston Prime''' is the [[Prime]] variant and direct upgrade of the {{Weapon|Burston}}, sporting higher stats across the board including fire rate, damage, status, and critical chance.

==Characteristics==

* This weapon deals primarily {{D|Slash}} damage.

{{Advantages|class=Rifle|trigger=Burst|* Can use the Burston Prime-exclusive {{M|Gilded Truth}}.|name=Burston Prime}}

{{Disadvantages|name=Burston Prime|class=Rifle|trigger=Burst|}}

{{WeaponComparison|Burston}}

{{PrimeTable}}
==Crafting==

The Burston Prime can be sold for {{cc|7,500}}.

== Incarnon Genesis ==
{{Transclude|Burston Incarnon Genesis#Acquisition}}

{{Transclude|Burston Incarnon Genesis#Incarnon Genesis}}

==Tips==
*The Burston Prime has a fast burst, making it decent in long-range combat.
*The Burston has arguably better ammo efficiency than the {{Weapon|Soma}} or {{Weapon|Synapse}} due to its burst-fire nature.
*Fire rate mods ({{M|Speed Trigger}}, {{M|Shred}}, {{M|Gilded Truth}}, etc.) reduce the delay between bursts, but did not increase the fire rate of the actual bullets themselves. As of {{ver|17.4.3}}, fire rate mods now increase the fire rate of the burst itself.
*It isn't advised to put a {{M|Heavy Caliber}} on the Burston Prime as this weapon benefits more in close to mid range situations with its high accuracy and damage over long range situations where hitting enemies with all bullets becomes more difficult.
*Modifying the magazine can sometimes be problematic, as you might be reduced to only 1 or 2 rounds in your last shot. A Max Rank {{M|Wildfire}} or a Rank 3 {{M|Magazine Warp}} will give you a magazine of 54, allowing you 18 bursts before reloading. This ensures you will always fire 3 rounds in every burst.

==Trivia==

*The Burston Prime has noticeably less golden ornamentation than previous [[Prime]] weapons.
*At the time of its release, the Burston Prime was the first Prime weapon whose component drops were exclusive to the [[Orokin Derelict]] instead of the [[Orokin Void]]. [[Update 12]] has since moved some component drops into the Void.
*The Burston Prime is the first Prime primary weapon to receive a [[Weapon Augments]] mod.
*The Burston Prime's gold parts can be recolored as of {{ver|15.13}}.
*During a flashback to [[The Old War]] in [[Erra (Quest)]], an {{WF|Excalibur Prime}} is seen wielding the Burston Prime, albeit firing in full-auto mode. This implies that the weapon was more powerful in the past, matching the weapon's Codex entry.

{{Codex|Mark your targets and then unleash a barrage of bullets, the Buzlok's homing rounds always find the enemy. Marked Targets are more likely to take critical hits.}}
The '''Buzlok''' is a {{Faction|Grineer}} slug assault rifle with unique homing capabilities. Its [[Alternate Fire]] launches a tracer round that sticks to NPCs or enemies, making all subsequent shots home in on the marked target. Successful homing shots gain a [[critical chance]] bonus.

==Characteristics==

* This weapon primarily deals {{D|Impact}} damage on its primary fire.
*[[Alternate Fire]] shoots a tracer round projectile that makes primary fire shoot [[homing]] rounds on the tracked entity, lasting '''20''' seconds or until target death.
*Successfully landing a tracer round grants a '''20''' second buff that adds '''50%''' ''absolute'' [[critical chance]]. This buff is retained on target death, and is not affected by mods.
{{Advantages||name=Buzlok}}
** Tracer round mechanic allows for free aiming, and shooting around cover to strike targets.

{{Disadvantages|* Once a target is selected with tracking beacon, the weapon will fire on that target until the beacon disappears or the enemy is killed, making it difficult to use against multiple targets or change targets.
* Has a unique Z-axis recoil, which creates irregular aimed accuracy after firing a burst.|name=Buzlok}}
*Projectiles have travel time on main fire and tracer round which may make tagging a weak spot difficult at range.

==Acquisition==
The Buzlok's blueprint can be [[research]]ed from the [[Research/Chem Lab|Chem Lab]] in the [[dojo]].

{{BuildAutomatic|type=Weapon}}
This weapon can be sold for {{cc|7,500}}.

==Notes ==

*Firing the tracking beacon consumes 1 ammo.
*[[Multishot]] bullets all land in the same area as the original shot.
* The tracking beacon will '''not''' affect enemies or allies under the effect of invisibility, such as [[Corpus Target]]s.
*Absolute 50% critical chance occurs after mods. i.e {{M|Point Strike}} with the buff active is (23 + (23 * 1.5)) + 50 = 107.5% critical chance.
*The alternate fire is affected by the critical chance buff.
*[[Multishot]] and [[Punch Through]] mods do '''not''' affect the tracking beacon.
*Beacons have projectile travel time, which may make it difficult to initially tag moving enemies at longer ranges.
**The beacons however have a speed roughly a third higher in comparison to the unguided rounds.
*The beacon can attach to any living entity, friend or foe.
*Homing rounds have good maneuverability, allowing them to hit targets behind cover, and even directly behind the player if angled properly and there is enough space for the bullet to maneuver. Nonetheless, they will still travel the fastest route to the target, and may thus occasionally hit walls and other obstacles.
**Homing rounds will travel straight for at least the first '''5''' meters before they begin homing towards the beacon.
**The homing rounds have a maximum deflection angle of 90 degrees from the direction of aim after being fired.
**Homing rounds will punch through an enemy in the direction the rounds hit.
* When used with {{WF|Mirage}}'s {{A|Hall of Mirrors}}, each illusory copy of the Buzlok will fire its own tracking beacon. However, the homing rounds from every copy will '''''NOT''''' home in on the player's tracking beacon. Each copy's rounds will home in on their own respective beacon. If the tracking beacon is active by launching before activating Hall of Mirrors, or if the copies' beacons do not hit a valid target to home in on, their rounds will instead fly straight and unguided.
** Each of Mirage's copies can simultaneously fire either homing or unguided rounds, depending on whether or not they have a valid beacon target to home in on.
**This is very easy to observe in the [[Simulacrum]] or [[Captura]] by firing at enemies with AI turned off.
*The flight time of unguided rounds is significantly faster than that of rounds homing in on a beacon.
**This is easily noticed when using Mirage's Hall Of Mirrors due to the previously described fact, as any unguided rounds fired by Mirage's copies will land much sooner than the homing rounds, despite being fired at the same time.
* If a tagged enemy goes invisible, it will disable the beacon.
*{{M|Heavy Caliber}} has no negative effect on the primary fire on this weapon when using it alongside a tagged beacon, however the beacon is still affected by the accuracy penalty.
* After a projectile hits the target, it loses its homing function. Therefore, punched-through projectiles will '''not''' re-home on a target.

== Tips==

*The Buzlok's homing nature provides several interesting use cases:
**Since the Buzlok can fire around corners to hit targets from complete cover, it is especially useful against [[Hellion]]s, [[Bombard]]s, and [[Napalm]]s. They can be quickly tagged between their shots, then safely eliminated.
**As the Buzlok's homing rounds home in precisely to the tracker, it is a great choice for headshot-based mods and arcanes such as [[Primary Deadhead]], [[Argon Scope]] / [[Galvanized Scope]], [[Arcane Rage]], and [[Arcane Victory]].
***[[Harrow]]'s [[Covenant]] buff is also quite powerful on the Buzlok, reaching +200% extra base Critical Chance on headshots. This is especially the case with [[Lasting Covenant]].
**The Buzlok is a great weapon for damaging fast moving enemies that may prove difficult to hit, such as the [[Manic]], [[Manic Bombard]], [[Stalker]], [[Acolytes]] or [[Zanuka Hunter]].
**The homing feature combined with the Buzlok's large magazine and good range means that it is surprisingly well suited to open-world areas (such as the [[Plains of Eidolon]] or the [[Orb Vallis]]).
**The homing projectiles will do extra damage on the "weak spots" made by {{WF|Banshee}}'s {{A|Sonar}} ability. However, this is very difficult to achieve since the bullets only home in after having traveled a couple of meters and will often hit other parts of the enemy before hitting the weak spot. Positioning is key to get the best out of this combination.
*{{M|Metal Auger}} and/or {{M|Shred}} are most useful on the Buzlok due to their punch-through abilities, allowing the homing rounds to hit tagged enemies behind cover.
**Alternatively aiming high towards the ceiling/sky will make the homing rounds take a more curved trajectory and hit the target from above, bypassing their cover.

==Trivia==

*The Grineer text on the side of the gun translates to "DO NOT TOUC" but is missing an "H" at the end to spell TOUCH.
* This is the first ever weapon to have a homing ability that can be used by players.
* Prior to {{ver|20}}, the Buzlok's beacon was triggered from [[zoom]]ed fire.
*This is the third Grineer weapon to bear "lok" at the end of its name, the first being the {{Weapon|Grinlok}} and second being the {{Weapon|Marelok}}.
*The Buzlok's projectiles are miniature missiles; on impact they give off tiny explosions. This is a purely cosmetic effect.
*As with the {{Weapon|Vectis}} and {{Weapon|Vectis Prime}}, the Buzlok is able to reload whilst scoped in, making it one of the three weapons able to do so.
*As with all projectiles with flight time, the Buzlok's projectiles will be affected by Ivara's Navigator.
**The homing beacon under the effect of Ivara's Navigator will pass through all obstacles until it hits an enemy or when the ability is ended. This can be used at the start of a mission to scout through the entire tileset without stepping foot in it.
* Oddly, the Buzlok's homing projectile is unable to lock onto [[Plant]]s found within [[Earth]], [[Fragments]] and [[Resources|Resource deposits]].
**Additionally, when fired upon a Resource deposit, it will do minimal damage usually just breaking single digits.
*Oddly, the Buzlok is situationally affected by flight speed mods; it will only apply them if firing unguided rounds or the tracer rounds and not when homing onto a tracer round's beacon.
*The Buzlok is unique in the fact that unlike all other weapons within Warframe, additional bullets caused by multishot mods will all land in exactly the same place, regardless if there is a tracking beacon or not.

*In the ''GHOULS'' comic, the Buzlok is wielded by Little Duck.
**she also [[Little Duck/Quotes|mentions it]] when you guild an [[amp]]
*Tied with {{Weapon|Prisma Grakata}} for the second highest [[critical multiplier]] of all fully automatic rifles, behind {{Weapon|Tiberon Prime}}, {{Weapon|Soma}}/{{Weapon|Soma Prime}}, and {{Weapon|Baza}}/{{Weapon|Baza Prime}}.


==Bugs ==

*When firing a tracking beacon with the camera view reversed (I.e. looking over your Warframe's left shoulder) the shot will not line up with the reticle. It will instead drift off to the right.
*If a tracker has been shot at a disappearing object, such as {{WF|Frost}}'s {{A|Snow Globe}} when its duration runs out, it will remain attached to nothing until its timer runs out.
* As of {{ver|16}}, the energy trails of each projectile fired by the Buzlok will disappear randomly throughout missions and will remain broken the remainder of the mission.
*When enemies affected by [[Void Fissure|Void fissure corruption]] are tagged, the Buzlok's scope will display "Corrupted |Enemy| tagged" instead of their actual name.
*After a second has passed of being fired, Buzlok projectiles will lose its energy trail effect while still capable of homing on its target.
*After the [[Tenet Diplos]] were added the Buzlok's tracer round broke entirely and after two hotfixes, it now can miss tagged targets significantly more than before, partly due to the tracer round now sometimes sticking out far enough from the enemy mesh that the rounds don't hit anything when passing through.
